description: The birch brand of Multi-brand: its theme picks in each mode. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

birch.label: Birch
birch.description: Friendly and helpful: violet, Plus Jakarta Sans, soft corners.

theme.$description: The Birch theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base. Info uses blue, kept apart from the brand color so it never reads as an action. Categories 1 to 5 are teal, purple, orange, blue, green: distinct hues for tags and chart series, with no meaning. Disabled uses the neutral slate.

open-ds.why: radius.12: We use a 12px corner for Birch's buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a friendly tone, by brand convention. A rounded radius does this by curving the edge clearly while the box keeps straight sides. So Birch feels softer than Aster yet still precise enough to fill a form, because each brand sets its corners (shape.values) on a neutral base (brand.q1).

radius.pill: We use a pill corner for Birch's badges in order to give status a role of its own, apart from the 12px controls. A full radius does this by rounding both ends into a capsule. So a status and a button never look alike, because each brand sets three corners (shape.roles) and Birch rounds its badges (shape.values).

radius.12: We use a 12px corner for Birch's menu options in order to keep nesting by the relation: the 16px surface corner minus the panel's 4px padding. The inner radius does this by the nesting rule of Aster's option corner, run 4px inside Birch's 16px surface. So an option's curve runs parallel to its menu's curve, because Birch's surfaces take 16px (shape.roles, brand.q1) and the panel's padding is 4px (spacing.values).

radius.12: We use the 12px control corner for Birch's growing boxes in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving Birch's list items and text areas the 12px curve of its controls. So fields and rows read as one family, because Birch's control corner is rounded, not a pill (shape.values).

radius.16: We use a 16px corner for Birch's cards and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a friendly tone by brand convention. A larger radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 12px controls. So a plan card reads as one soft object, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and each brand colors a neutral base (brand.q1).
